rules.statement: The donation by a spouse to another is not fraudulent merely because the donor desires to safeguard the property gifted against being made liable for his debts, and the donated property should be subject to the debts of the donor only at the time of the alienation.
rules.supporting_quote: It seems to me that, in the present case, the evidence against the 2nd defendant cannot be put higher than this, that he desired to safeguard the property gifted to his wife against being made liable for his debts, or at any rate for the results of the litigation on which he was about to embark. That is not sufficient to make the alienation fraudulent, in the absence of affirmative proof that he had no other poperty against which his creditors could have recourse.
